description: Status block, 62 registers from 0x0000, as the official app sends it to the balancer. Reply: D2 03 7C, 129 bytes.

Status block, 80 registers from 0x0000 (165 byte reply). cepr polls 20S and 24S balancers with it over the UART port every 500 ms and lists "the balancer answers the 80-register read" as confirmed on hardware. Frame bytes as printed in both sources.
Nine registers from 0x003E (balancing bits, balance current, MOSFET and board temperature on newer BMS firmware). Read by the app on every cycle of its balancer page.
Settings block, 41 registers from 0x0080 (87 byte reply). Read first after connecting and on every cycle of the balancer page.
Version block, 32 registers from 0x00A9 (software, hardware, machine code).
Parameter password, 3 registers from 0x00C9. The app compares the user input with it locally.
Two registers from 0x00CC (production date), read once per session.
Five registers from 0x00CC: production date, 0x00CE, balancer switch 0x00CF, 0x00D0. Read on every cycle of the balancer page; the only read of the switch state by the app.

description: Balancer switch register 0x00CF alone. Not sent by the official app, which reads it inside the 0x00CC block.
Seventeen registers from 0x00DF, read by the app on its balancer page; this balancer answers with 0xFFFF only.
Register 0x00D7, read once by the app (answer 0, meaning unknown).
Twelve registers from 0x0057 (GPS block on BMS boards), read once per app session.
Twenty-eight registers from 0x0063, read once per app session (all 0xFFFF on this balancer).

Single register read of 0x0089 (battery type). cepr read these registers one at a time over the UART port of a real balancer and every request was answered with a valid CRC (reply D2 03 02 <value> <CRC>, 7 bytes); the request bytes are computed.

Single register read of 0x008A (sleep wait time). cepr read these registers one at a time over the UART port of a real balancer and every request was answered with a valid CRC (reply D2 03 02 <value> <CRC>, 7 bytes); the request bytes are computed.

Single register read of 0x00A3 (balance start voltage). cepr read these registers one at a time over the UART port of a real balancer and every request was answered with a valid CRC (reply D2 03 02 <value> <CRC>, 7 bytes); the request bytes are computed.

Single register read of 0x00A4 (balance start voltage difference). cepr read these registers one at a time over the UART port of a real balancer and every request was answered with a valid CRC (reply D2 03 02 <value> <CRC>, 7 bytes); the request bytes are computed.

Single register read of 0x00A8 (register 0x00A8, meaning unconfirmed on balancers). cepr read these registers one at a time over the UART port of a real balancer and every request was answered with a valid CRC (reply D2 03 02 <value> <CRC>, 7 bytes); the request bytes are computed.
Balancer off (0x00CF = 0), written by the app. Echoed 179 ms later; the next 0x00CC block read shows 0x00CF = 0.
Balancer on (0x00CF = 1). The first echo arrived with a bad CRC and the app wrote again after 10 s; the next read shows 0x00CF = 1.

Sleep wait time 65535 s = never sleep, the value the Daly manual gives to cancel sleep. cepr reports that a write to 0x008A on a real balancer was echoed (value not stated). Frame bytes as printed in both sources.
Sleep wait time 3600 s (factory default per the Daly balancer manual). CRC computed.
Balance start voltage 3300 mV (factory default of the UART/RS485 model). Register read on two balancers; no write to it is captured on a balancer, so ubms verifies by read-back.
Balance start voltage difference 20 mV (factory default). Register read on two balancers; no write to it is captured on a balancer, so ubms verifies by read-back.
